from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with the title and lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            'Meet Pixel the Cat on a 2D grid.',
            "Transformations stretch or shrink Pixel's world.",
            'The determinant measures this change in area.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Transformation Factor", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight Line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # Create a coordinate grid and "Pixel" (the square)
        # We build them around (0,0) then move the whole group to the display area
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        # Define a small 2x2 grid (from -1 to 2) to allow for stretching space
        for x in range(-1, 3):
            grid_lines.add(Line([x, -1, 0], [x, 2, 0], color=GREY, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.5))
        for y in range(-1, 3):
            grid_lines.add(Line([-1, y, 0], [2, y, 0], color=GREY, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.5))
        
        # Pixel is a 1x1 Cyan square
        pixel = Rectangle(
            width=1, 
            height=1, 
            stroke_color="#00FFFF", 
            fill_color="#00FFFF", 
            fill_opacity=0.3
        )
        # Position Pixel so its bottom-left corner is at (0,0)
        pixel.move_to([0.5, 0.5, 0])
        
        # A tracker point to identify the grid origin (0,0) for the transformation
        origin_tracker = Dot(point=[0, 0, 0], fill_opacity=0)
        
        # Group components together
        visual_group = VGroup(grid_lines, pixel, origin_tracker)
        
        # Position the group in the lower part of the 6x6 workspace (C1 to F6)
        # This leaves the top part (A-B rows) for labels
        self.place_in_area(visual_group, "C1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_lines), FadeIn(pixel))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight Line 2
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # Matrix transformation: Scale x by 3 and y by 2 (Area becomes 1*3*2 = 6)
        transformation_matrix = np.array([
            [3, 0, 0],
            [0, 2, 0],
            [0, 0, 1]
        ])

        # Animate the stretch around the origin tracker's center
        self.play(
            visual_group.animate.apply_matrix(
                transformation_matrix, 
                about_point=origin_tracker.get_center()
            ),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight Line 3
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # Highlight the final area in yellow
        self.play(
            pixel.animate.set_fill("#FFFF00", opacity=0.6).set_stroke("#FFFF00"),
            run_time=1
        )

        # Labels for the transformation
        factor_label = Text("Area Scale Factor: 6", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        det_label = Text("det(A) = 6", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        
        # Positioning labels in the top area of the grid system
        self.place_at_grid(factor_label, "A2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(det_label, "A5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(
            Write(factor_label),
            Write(det_label)
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Prerequisite Knowledge: Basis Vectors"
        lines = [
            'Unit vectors i-hat and j-hat define space.',
            'Matrices track where these basis vectors land.',
            "These positions determine the new grid's shape."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Helper to create a bracketed matrix without Tex
        def create_matrix(a, c, b, d, color=WHITE):
            content = VGroup(
                VGroup(Text(str(a), font_size=24), Text(str(c), font_size=24)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5),
                VGroup(Text(str(b), font_size=24), Text(str(d), font_size=24)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
            
            bracket_l = Text("[", font_size=60).scale(1.2).next_to(content, LEFT, buff=0.1)
            bracket_r = Text("]", font_size=60).scale(1.2).next_to(content, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
            matrix = VGroup(content, bracket_l, bracket_r).set_color(color)
            return matrix

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a small local coordinate system on the grid
        # Center the plane at D3-E4 area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B2', 'F5')
        
        # i-hat (1,0) - Red
        i_hat = Arrow(
            start=plane.coords_to_point(0, 0),
            end=plane.coords_to_point(1, 0),
            buff=0,
            color="#FF0000"
        )
        i_label = Text("i", font_size=18, color="#FF0000").next_to(i_hat, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # j-hat (0,1) - Green
        j_hat = Arrow(
            start=plane.coords_to_point(0, 0),
            end=plane.coords_to_point(0, 1),
            buff=0,
            color="#00FF00"
        )
        j_label = Text("j", font_size=18, color="#00FF00").next_to(j_hat, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(plane), GrowArrow(i_hat), GrowArrow(j_hat), FadeIn(i_label), FadeIn(j_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Matrix values
        a, b = 2, 1
        c, d = 0, 2
        
        matrix_obj = create_matrix("a", "c", "b", "d", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_obj, 'A4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Highlight columns for i-hat and j-hat
        col1_rect = SurroundingRectangle(matrix_obj[0][0], color="#FF0000", buff=0.1)
        col2_rect = SurroundingRectangle(matrix_obj[0][1], color="#00FF00", buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_obj))
        self.play(Create(col1_rect))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(col1_rect, col2_rect))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(col2_rect))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Destination points
        target_i = plane.coords_to_point(a, b)
        target_j = plane.coords_to_point(c, d)
        
        # Generic to concrete matrix labels
        concrete_matrix = create_matrix(str(a), str(c), str(b), str(d), color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(concrete_matrix, 'A4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Transform labels and vectors
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(matrix_obj, concrete_matrix))
        
        self.play(
            i_hat.animate.put_start_and_end_on(plane.coords_to_point(0, 0), target_i),
            j_hat.animate.put_start_and_end_on(plane.coords_to_point(0, 0), target_j),
            i_label.animate.next_to(target_i, RIGHT, buff=0.1),
            j_label.animate.next_to(target_j, UP, buff=0.1),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Visualizing the "shape" - simple parallelogram
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            plane.coords_to_point(0, 0),
            target_i,
            plane.coords_to_point(a + c, b + d),
            target_j,
            stroke_width=2,
            fill_opacity=0.2,
            color=BLUE
        )
        
        self.play(Create(parallelogram))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            'Start with a unit square of area one.',
            'Basis vectors transform into a parallelogram shape.',
            "The determinant is this parallelogram's area.",
            'Scaling one vector by three triples the area.',
            'All areas scale by this single constant factor.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Geometric Definition (2D)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid Coordinates Reference
        # Origin will be 'D3'
        origin = self.grid['D3']
        unit_x = self.grid['D4'] - origin
        unit_y = self.grid['C3'] - origin

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Simple axes
        x_axis = Line(origin - unit_x, origin + 3.5*unit_x, color=GRAY, stroke_width=1)
        y_axis = Line(origin - unit_y, origin + 2.5*unit_y, color=GRAY, stroke_width=1)
        
        # Vectors and unit square
        i_vec = Arrow(start=origin, end=origin + unit_x, buff=0, color="#FF4444")
        j_vec = Arrow(start=origin, end=origin + unit_y, buff=0, color="#44FF44")
        i_label = Text("i", font_size=20, color="#FF4444")
        j_label = Text("j", font_size=20, color="#44FF44")
        self.place_at_grid(i_label, "E4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(j_label, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        unit_square = Polygon(
            origin, 
            origin + unit_x, 
            origin + unit_x + unit_y, 
            origin + unit_y, 
            color=WHITE, 
            stroke_width=2
        )
        
        self.add(x_axis, y_axis)
        self.play(Create(unit_square), GrowArrow(i_vec), GrowArrow(j_vec), FadeIn(i_label), FadeIn(j_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # New basis vectors: i=(2, 0.5), j=(0.5, 1.5)
        new_i_pt = origin + 2*unit_x + 0.5*unit_y
        new_j_pt = origin + 0.5*unit_x + 1.5*unit_y
        new_sum_pt = origin + 2.5*unit_x + 2.0*unit_y
        
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            origin,
            new_i_pt,
            new_sum_pt,
            new_j_pt,
            color="#FFFF00",
            stroke_width=3
        )
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(unit_square, parallelogram),
            i_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin, new_i_pt),
            j_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin, new_j_pt),
            i_label.animate.move_to(self.grid["E5"]),
            j_label.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Fill the parallelogram with 50% opacity yellow
        parallelogram.set_fill("#FFFF00", opacity=0.5)
        self.play(parallelogram.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.5))
        
        # Flash Text Area = |Determinant|
        area_text = Text("Area = |Determinant|", font_size=28, color="#FFFFFF", weight=BOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(area_text, "A4")
        self.play(Flash(area_text, color=WHITE))
        self.add(area_text)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(TEAL)
        
        # Clean up and reset for next example
        self.play(
            FadeOut(parallelogram),
            FadeOut(area_text),
            i_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin, origin + unit_x),
            j_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin, origin + unit_y),
            i_label.animate.move_to(self.grid["E4"]),
            j_label.animate.move_to(self.grid["C2"]),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Show scaling i-vector by 3
        scaled_i_pt = origin + 3*unit_x
        scaling_rect = Polygon(
            origin,
            scaled_i_pt,
            scaled_i_pt + unit_y,
            origin + unit_y,
            color=TEAL,
            fill_color=TEAL,
            fill_opacity=0.4,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        
        self.play(
            i_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin, scaled_i_pt),
            i_label.animate.move_to(self.grid["E6"]),
            Create(scaling_rect),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        scale_label = Text("Area triples (3x)", font_size=22, color=TEAL)
        self.place_at_grid(scale_label, "B4")
        self.play(Write(scale_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFD700") # Gold
        
        # Show a circle being scaled along with the space
        # Small circle in original unit area
        small_circle = Circle(radius=0.2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        self.place_in_area(small_circle, 'C3', 'D4')
        
        # Scaled circle (ellipse) in the 3x1 rect
        scaled_ellipse = Ellipse(width=1.2, height=0.4, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(scaled_ellipse, 'C3', 'D6')
        
        self.play(Create(small_circle))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(small_circle, scaled_ellipse))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "The Formula: ad - bc"
        lines = [
            'The standard determinant formula is ad minus bc.',
            "Terms 'a' and 'd' represent primary diagonal scaling.",
            "'b' and 'c' account for the grid's shear.",
            'Algebraically, this calculates the area of the parallelogram.',
            'The formula perfectly matches our geometric intuition.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_A = "#58C4DD" # Blue
        COLOR_B = "#FC6255" # Red
        COLOR_C = "#FC6255" # Red
        COLOR_D = "#58C4DD" # Blue
        COLOR_PARA = "#77B05D" # Green
        COLOR_BOX = GRAY_B

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        f1 = Text("det(A) = ", font_size=32)
        f2 = Text("a", color=COLOR_A, font_size=32)
        f3 = Text("d", color=COLOR_D, font_size=32)
        f4 = Text(" - ", font_size=32)
        f5 = Text("b", color=COLOR_B, font_size=32)
        f6 = Text("c", color=COLOR_C, font_size=32)
        formula = VGroup(f1, f2, f3, f4, f5, f6).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_A)
        
        # Grid/Example values
        a, b, c, d = 2.0, 1.0, 1.0, 3.0
        s = 0.55 
        origin = self.grid['E2'] + LEFT * 0.5 + DOWN * 0.5
        
        p0 = origin
        p1 = origin + np.array([a*s, b*s, 0])
        p2 = origin + np.array([c*s, d*s, 0])
        p3 = origin + np.array([(a+c)*s, (b+d)*s, 0])
        
        parallelogram = Polygon(p0, p1, p3, p2, color=COLOR_PARA, fill_opacity=0.3)
        label_a = Text("a", color=COLOR_A, font_size=20).next_to(p0 + np.array([a*s/2, 0, 0]), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_d = Text("d", color=COLOR_D, font_size=20).next_to(p0 + np.array([0, d*s/2, 0]), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        diag_a = Line(p0, p0 + np.array([a*s, 0, 0]), color=COLOR_A, stroke_width=4)
        diag_d = Line(origin + np.array([0, d*s, 0]), origin, color=COLOR_D, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(
            Create(parallelogram),
            Create(diag_a),
            Create(diag_d),
            FadeIn(label_a),
            FadeIn(label_d)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_B)
        
        label_b = Text("b", color=COLOR_B, font_size=20).next_to(p1, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        label_c = Text("c", color=COLOR_C, font_size=20).next_to(p2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        shear_b = Line(p1, p1 - np.array([0, b*s, 0]), color=COLOR_B, stroke_width=4)
        shear_c = Line(p2, p2 - np.array([c*s, 0, 0]), color=COLOR_C, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(
            Create(shear_b),
            Create(shear_c),

    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with specified lines
        lines = [
            'Consider a matrix where both columns are identical.',
            'The entire 2D plane collapses onto a single line.',
            "Pixel's area is squashed down to zero.",
            'A zero determinant means the transformation cannot be reversed.',
            'Information is lost when dimensions are lost.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Zero Determinant: The Collapse", lines)

        # Matrix [1 1; 1 1] construction
        col1 = VGroup(Text("1", font_size=24), Text("1", font_size=24)).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
        col2 = VGroup(Text("1", font_size=24), Text("1", font_size=24)).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
        matrix_vals = VGroup(col1, col2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.6)
        bracket_l = Text("[", font_size=40)
        bracket_r = Text("]", font_size=40)
        matrix_display = VGroup(bracket_l, matrix_vals, bracket_r).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Grid construction for the coordinate area
        # Anchor the origin at D4
        origin = self.grid["D4"]
        unit = 0.8
        
        def to_local(p):
            return origin + np.array([p[0]*unit, p[1]*unit, 0])

        # Initial state elements
        plane_grid = VGroup()
        for i in range(-2, 3):
            plane_grid.add(Line(to_local([-2, i]), to_local([2, i]), color=GRAY, stroke_opacity=0.4))
            plane_grid.add(Line(to_local([i, -2]), to_local([i, 2]), color=GRAY, stroke_opacity=0.4))
            
        i_hat = Arrow(origin, to_local([1, 0]), buff=0, color=PINK, stroke_width=4)
        j_hat = Arrow(origin, to_local([0, 1]), buff=0, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
        
        # Pixel the Cat / Unit Square (Cyan #00FFFF)
        pixel_square = Polygon(
            to_local([0,0]), to_local([1,0]), to_local([1,1]), to_local([0,1]),
            fill_opacity=0.5, fill_color="#00FFFF", stroke_color="#00FFFF"
        )

        # Transformation logic: (x,y) -> (x+y, x+y)
        # Target state elements
        t_i_hat = Arrow(origin, to_local([1, 1]), buff=0, color=PINK, stroke_width=4)
        t_j_hat = Arrow(origin, to_local([1, 1]), buff=0, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
        
        # The cyan square collapses to a line segment from (0,0) to (2,2)
        collapsed_pixel = Line(to_local([0,0]), to_local([2,2]), color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=6)

        # Collapsed grid lines
        collapsed_grid = VGroup()
        for i in range(-4, 5):
            # All lines collapse onto the y=x diagonal in local space
            # We represent the "density" of the collapsed plane as a thickened line
            collapsed_grid.add(Line(to_local([-2, -2]), to_local([2, 2]), color=GRAY, stroke_opacity=0.2))

        # Labels

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_display, "A4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(plane_grid, pixel_square, i_hat, j_hat)
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_display), FadeIn(plane_grid), FadeIn(pixel_square), FadeIn(i_hat), FadeIn(j_hat))
        self.wait(1)

        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(plane_grid, collapsed_grid),
            ReplacementTransform(i_hat, t_i_hat),
            ReplacementTransform(j_hat, t_j_hat),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Pixel's area is squashed down to zero."

        self.wait(1)

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial layout setup
        lines = [
            "The determinant is space's fundamental scaling factor.",
            "In 3D, it measures changes in volume.",
            "It defines how matrices reshape our universe."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and 3D Intuition", lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show '2D: Area Scale' vs '3D: Volume Scale' text
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        text_2d = Text("2D: Area Scale", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        text_3d = Text("3D: Volume Scale", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(text_2d, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(text_3d, "B5")
        
        # Simple 2D square to show area scaling
        square = Square(side_length=1.0, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        rect = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.7, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(square, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(rect, "C2") # To be used in transform
        
        self.play(FadeIn(text_2d), FadeIn(text_3d), Create(square))
        self.play(Transform(square, rect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw a 2D projection of a unit cube transforming into a parallelepiped.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(TEAL))
        
        # Cube vertices in 3D
        vertices_cube = [
            np.array([0, 0, 0]), np.array([1, 0, 0]), np.array([1, 1, 0]), np.array([0, 1, 0]),
            np.array([0, 0, 1]), np.array([1, 0, 1]), np.array([1, 1, 1]), np.array([0, 1, 1])
        ]
        
        # Parallelepiped vertices (skewed transformation)
        vertices_para = [
            np.array([0, 0, 0]), np.array([1.2, 0.1, 0]), np.array([1.4, 0.9, 0]), np.array([0.2, 0.8, 0]),
            np.array([0.3, 0.2, 1.1]), np.array([1.5, 0.3, 1.1]), np.array([1.7, 1.1, 1.1]), np.array([0.5, 1.0, 1.1])
        ]

        def get_projection(points):
            # Projection: (x, y, z) -> (x + 0.4z, y + 0.2z)
            projected = []
            for p in points:
                projected.append(np.array([p[0] + 0.4 * p[2], p[1] + 0.2 * p[2], 0]))
            return projected

        proj_cube = get_projection(vertices_cube)
        proj_para = get_projection(vertices_para)
        
        edges = [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 0), (4, 5), (5, 6), (6, 7), (7, 4), (0, 4), (1, 5), (2, 6), (3, 7)]
        
        cube_lines = VGroup(*[Line(proj_cube[i], proj_cube[j], color=GREEN) for i, j in edges])
        para_lines = VGroup(*[Line(proj_para[i], proj_para[j], color=GREEN) for i, j in edges])
        
        # Group and scale/position
        cube_group = cube_lines.scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(cube_group, "D4", "F6")
        
        # Sync para_lines to same position/scale as cube_group for smooth transition
        para_group = para_lines.scale(0.8).move_to(cube_group.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(cube_group))
        self.play(Transform(cube_group, para_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade out with text 'Determinant: The Scaling Factor of Space'
        # Fixed NameError: Changed undefined MAGENTA to PURPLE
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        
        summary_text = Text("Determinant:\nThe Scaling Factor of Space", font_size=32, color=WHITE, t2c={"Determinant": YELLOW})
        self.place_in_area(summary_text, "B1", "E6")
        
        # Clear area then show final message
        self.play(
            FadeOut(text_2d), FadeOut(text_3d), FadeOut(square), FadeOut(cube_group)
        )
        self.play(Write(summary_text))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Determinant: The Scaling Factor of Space
outline.target_audience: University STEM students or Advanced High School students

sections.title: Introduction: The Transformation Factor
sections.content: Hook the audience by framing the determinant not as a formula, but as a 'scaling factor' for space. Introduce a character, 'Pixel the Cat,' living on a 2D grid. When a linear transformation is applied, Pixel's world stretches or shrinks. The determinant tells us exactly how much Pixel's area changes.
sections.example: If Pixel occupies a 1x1 square (Area = 1) and a transformation makes him occupy an area of 6, the determinant of that transformation matrix is 6.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Basis Vectors
sections.content: Briefly review the unit basis vectors i-hat (1,0) and j-hat (0,1). Explain that any 2x2 matrix describes where these two vectors land after a transformation. Visualizing these landing spots is the key to understanding the resulting shape.
sections.example: In a matrix [a, c; b, d], the first column (a, b) is where i-hat lands, and the second column (c, d) is where j-hat lands.

sections.title: The Geometric Definition (2D)
sections.content: Show that the unit square formed by i-hat and j-hat transforms into a parallelogram. The area of this parallelogram is the absolute value of the determinant. Use an animation to transition from the 1x1 square to the skewed parallelogram.
sections.example: A matrix [3, 0; 0, 2] stretches i-hat by 3 and j-hat by 2. The 1x1 square becomes a 3x2 rectangle. The area is 6, so the determinant is 6.

sections.title: The Formula: ad - bc
sections.content: Connect the geometric area to the standard algebraic formula det(A) = ad - bc. Use a color-coded diagram to show how the components of the vectors (a, b) and (c, d) interact to calculate the area of the parallelogram minus the 'excess' triangles.
sections.example: For a matrix [2, 1; 1, 3], calculate (2*3) - (1*1) = 5. Visually demonstrate that the resulting parallelogram covers exactly 5 square units on the grid.

sections.title: Orientation and Negative Determinants
sections.content: Explain what a negative determinant means. It represents a change in 'orientation' or 'handedness.' If the transformation flips the plane (like looking at Pixel the Cat in a mirror), the determinant becomes negative.
sections.example: If i-hat moves to the right of j-hat initially, but after transformation it ends up to the left of j-hat, the 'paper' of space has been flipped over. The determinant will be negative (e.g., -2).

sections.title: The Zero Determinant: The Collapse
sections.content: Discuss the critical case where the determinant is zero. This happens when the transformation squashes the entire 2D space onto a single line or a point. If the area is zero, the transformation is not invertible (you can't 'un-squash' a line back into a plane).
sections.example: A 'Black Hole' device matrix [1, 1; 1, 1] moves both basis vectors to the same diagonal line. Pixel the Cat is crushed into a 1D line with 0 area. Determinant = (1*1) - (1*1) = 0.

sections.title: Summary and 3D Intuition
sections.content: Wrap up by summarizing that the determinant is the 'Area Scaling Factor.' Briefly mention that in 3D, it represents the 'Volume Scaling Factor' for a parallelepiped.
sections.example: In a 3D video game, if a 3x3 transformation matrix has a determinant of 8, any 3D object (like a character model) will become 8 times more voluminous.

storyboard.title: The Zero Determinant: The Collapse
lecture_lines: Consider a matrix where both columns are identical.
The entire 2D plane collapses onto a single line.
Pixel's area is squashed down to zero.
A zero determinant means the transformation cannot be reversed.
Information is lost when dimensions are lost.
animations: Input matrix [[1, 1], [1, 1]] and show the unit square.
Animate the grid collapsing onto the diagonal line y = x.
Shrink the cyan #00FFFF square until it becomes a 1D line segment.
Label the collapsed line with 'Area = 0' in white #FFFFFF.
Display 'det(A) = 0: The transformation is not invertible' in red #FF0000.

storyboard.title: Summary and 3D Intuition
lecture_lines: Determinants scale area in 2D and volume in 3D.
They describe how matrices reshape the space around us.
Use the determinant to master the geometry of transformation.
animations: Show '2D: Area Scale' vs '3D: Volume Scale' text #FFFFFF.
Draw a 2D projection of a unit cube [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cube.svg] transforming into a parallelepiped.
Fade out with text 'Determinant: The Scaling Factor of Space' #FFFFFF.
